business_scope.primary_industry_name: Zinc Alloy Die-Casting and Tampo Printing of 1:18 Scale Car Replicas

EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Convention (DTA, 1996 as amended)
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement (1994 as amended by 2020 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Law of 12 November 2004 on the Fight against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) for Luxembourg partnerships and legal entities; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on RBE implementation; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of every ultimate corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national trade registry or corporate affairs authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement of all intermediate holding entities in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or company registry where the intermediate entities are registered

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual UBO passport copies and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority / local municipal records office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign beneficial ownership register or financial intelligence unit

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory name and ID screening of all partners, managers, and beneficial owners against the following indices before notarization: Luxembourg Ministry of Finance consolidated financial sanctions list, CSSF blacklists, European Union Common Foreign and Security Policy restrictive measures, US OFAC SDN and Consular, UN Security Council consolidated list, FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions list, and world-check politiclaly exposed persons databases. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, family member, close associate, or high-risk jurisdiction, with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. All screening findings must be evidenced in writing and retained in the legal onboarding file for at least five years after the business relationship ends, per the Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) electronic filing portal and LBR name availability search platform (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be distinguishable from existing registrations and shall not be contrary to public policy or misleading. The name may be expressed in Luxembourgish, French, German, English, or another language using the Latin alphabet; where the original uses non-Latin script, a mandatory statutory Latin transliteration must be filed and registered. The name must comply with order of the Luxembourg business registers regarding corporate suffixes; the phrase 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale' appears in the name, and a correct translation or transliteration is required for foreign-language names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant may within three months from notification file an administrative appeal with the President of the Administrative Tribunal (Président du Tribunal administratif) under the amended law of 21 June 1999 on administrative procedure. The applicant may alternatively file a new name reservation with a different distinguishing element. A reasonable extension of the initial 90-day reservation window may be sought before expiration by submitting a renewal request through the LBR portal, subject to a maximum of one additional 90-day period and payment of the applicable extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for a non-regulated commercial SCSp engaged in die-cast collectible distribution, provided that the SCSp maintains a registered office address in Luxembourg open during normal business hours for correspondence and service of process. The virtual office must be supplied by a reputable Luxembourg-licensed service provider or law firm. However, the virtual office alone cannot satisfy the commercial substance expectation of the Luxembourg tax authorities under OECD BEPS substance forms; for an active trading operation involving cargo, warehousing, and invoicing, the SCSp should keep physical contracts, employee or subcontractor evidence, and operational instructions available in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 5% for a low-risk die-cast model distribution entity without client facing financial services or regulated licenses. Unannounced on-site visits by the Luxembourg tax authorities, the FIU, and the Minister of Justice's office may still occur if financial anomalies, suspicious transaction reports, or adverse media are observed. The physical presence of a qualified Luxembourg domiciliation agent materially reduces the likelihood of an adverse inspection finding.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (especially Articles 32-34 and Article 100-1 et seq. inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016 establishing the SCSp); registration procedure governed by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Cité Judiciaire, Luxembourg City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société (partnership agreement) filed via the e-RCS electronic filing portal; legal notice published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital applies to a Luxembourg SCSp; partnership capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement, with no mandatory escrow account or statutory share capital deposit (Law of 23 July 2016).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: ORGANIZATIONAL RESOLUTION OF [SCSp NAME]. The partners hereby resolve that the subscription of partnership interests set out in the executed partnership agreement is ratified and recorded. The registered office is adopted at [address], Luxembourg, for an indefinite term. [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant) with the sole power to represent the SCSp both in judicial and extrajudicial matters, with full authority to file the partnership before the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, to register for VAT, social security, and the business establishment permit, to open bank accounts, to appoint professional advisers, and to bind the SCSp within the scope of ordinary business. The partnership agreement is confirmed in its entirety. This resolution is effective upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and legalization of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners' own execution; notary public only if immovable property is contributed; certification by Luxembourg Business Registers for legalization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement in French (or with a certified French translation), appointing a general partner (GP) and at least one limited partner (LP), with profit-sharing and governance clauses. Execute the deed as a private signed contract, or before a notary if real estate or certain transfers are involved. Attach identity documents, solvency declarations, and legality statements, and prepare a signed registered-office consent letter.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement (private deed or notarial act)
Passport copies of all general and limited partners
Declaration of non-bankruptcy for the manager (gérant) and corporate GP
Statement of legality of the die-casting manufacturing activity
Registered-office consent letter from the premises owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the deed, execute a supplementary rectification agreement or amendatory deed and resubmit for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS (e-RCS portal or registry desk at the Cité Judiciaire, Luxembourg City).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation e-filing on the Luxembourg Business Registers portal using Luxtrust/eID authentication. Attach the executed partnership agreement, complete the standardized RCS forms with details of the GP, LPs, registered office, and legal representative, and pay the official registration fee. Upon approval, obtain the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS electronic filing form
Original or certified copy of the partnership agreement
Proof of registered office (lease or owner consent)
Identity documents and residence permits of the manager (gérant)
Declaration on the lawful nature of the industrial activity
Bank confirmation of any capital contributions paid (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the RCS query within the given 15-day cure window, file corrected particulars or a rectification deed, and re-submit through the e-RCS portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal notice in the RESA official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), published by the Luxembourg Business Registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS registration is completed, the RCS automatically generates and publishes the statutory excerpt in RESA containing the SCSp's name, registered office, partners' liability details, and manager identity. Verify the published notice and download the certified RCS extract for banks, clients, and licensing authorities.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (auto-generated)
Partnership agreement excerpts for mandatory publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice contains errors, file a formal rectification request with the RCS and publish a corrective notice in RESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with the Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the employer registration file to the CCSS as soon as the SCSp hires staff, including employees of the die-casting plant. Obtain the employer identification number and affiliate workers to the Luxembourg social security scheme, covering sickness, pension, and accident insurance.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
CCSS employer registration form
Employee list with national identification numbers
Employment contracts and residence/work permits of staff
Manager identity document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused or delayed, self-file the form, pay any retroactive social contributions with a written justification, and request formal confirmation from the CCSS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) registration with the Luxembourg Registration Duties and VAT Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), VAT Department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Luxembourg VAT registration form (formulaire no. 763) describing the zinc alloy die-casting and tampo printing activity. Upon approval, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT number (format LU + 8 digits) and determines the monthly or quarterly filing cycle and Intrastat reporting obligations.
required_dossiers: VAT registration application form (no. 763)
RCS registration extract
Written description of the industrial and commercial activities
Estimated turnover declaration
Manager's identity document and power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incomplete information, supplement the file with the requested details and liaise directly with the AEDT team to obtain a written VAT registration confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Directorate General for Middle Classes (Direction générale des classes moyennes), Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment authorization dossier for the commercial and artisanal die-casting activity under the Law of 2 September 2011. Evidence the professional qualification of the manager or designated qualified manager in the metalworking/craft sector, the clean criminal record, and the Luxembourg registered office. Obtain the formal approval before commencement of operations.
required_dossiers: Autorisation d'établissement application form
Proof of professional qualification (diploma, apprenticeship certificate, or craft card)
Criminal record extract of the manager (casier judiciaire)
RCS extract of the SCSp and GP
Identity documents of the manager/GP
Proof of Luxembourg registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for lack of professional qualification or legal documentation, cure within the 14-day suspension period by submitting supplementary evidence or comments to the competent ministry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Directorate General for Industry and Middle Classes, in coordination with the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity for environmental permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement classé (commodo/incommodo environmental operating permit, Law of 15 June 1994) and Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment authorization, Law of 2 September 2011).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 1 'établissement classé' requiring prior authorization with a full environmental impact assessment (EIA report) where zinc/aluminium melting capacity reaches 20 tonnes per day or above; otherwise a Class 2 environmental registration (déclaration) with a simplified compliance notice.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Law of 15 June 1994 discharge limits: wastewater pH 6.5-8.5, total suspended solids not exceeding 60 mg/L, zinc below 2 mg/L, lead below 0.5 mg/L; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions under the EU Solvent Emissions Directive (1999/13/EC) applicable to metal coating and die-casting lines; zinc dross, skimmings, and sludge classified as hazardous waste and tracked per the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGIDS) covering evacuation routes, extinguishing systems, and molten-metal fire hazards; workplace clearance and structural-load inspection by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du travail et des mines) for die-casting presses, ventilation systems, ATEX zones, and occupational health compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT - Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority), Ministry of Finance, Luxembourg; electronic portal: Guichet.lu / MyGuichet (https://guichet.lu); direct income-tax classification administered by the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); export/customs controls by the Administration des douanes et accises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the SCSp (no minimum share capital required) and obtain the Luxembourg national identification number (NIF / RCSL registration) through the Luxembourg Business Registers. Step 2 - File VAT registration Form 645 (Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT, attaching the partnership agreement (contrat de société), RCSL extract, proof of registered office, identity documents of the general partner (gérant) and beneficial owners, and projected turnover by VAT rate; non-established SCSp must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative where required. Step 3 - AEDT issues a VAT identification number on the pattern 'LU' + 8 digits (e.g., LU12345678) within approximately 10-15 working days, effective from the date of first taxable supply. Step 4 - Maintain VAT records in Luxembourg and file periodic returns via MyGuichet; no separate direct-tax registration is required for the fiscally transparent partnership itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is statutorily transparent for income tax and is expressly excluded from the § 166 LIR election to be taxed as a corporation. Available elections: (i) VAT fiscal unity ('assujetti unique') under Article 60 of the 1979 VAT Law to group the SCSp with closely linked Luxembourg entities; (ii) waiver of the Article 57 small-business exemption (franchise) to recover input VAT and charge VAT on supplies; (iii) Union and non-Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) elections for distance sales of the die-cast models; (iv) option to apply customs inward-processing/export regimes designating the operating partner as exporter of record.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under Council Directive 2006/112/EC as transposed by the Luxembourg Law of 12 February 1979, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-business exemption: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (Article 57 of the 1979 VAT Law, 2024 threshold). Non-established taxable persons have no de minimis exemption and must register from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. Intra-Community distance sales of goods are subject to the EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold unless the OSS election is exercised.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping mandate. Statutory e-invoicing applies only to business-to-government (B2G) supplies: invoices to the Luxembourg State and public bodies must be structured EN 16931 electronic invoices (UBL/CII or PEPPOL BIS 3.0) transmitted via the PEPPOL network, per Directive 2014/55/EU. B2B/B2C e-invoicing is voluntary; paper, PDF, Factur-X and other agreed formats remain valid. The AEDT may request the Luxembourg Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T LS) in XML during a VAT audit, but no periodic SAF-T filing is imposed. Export invoices must state 'art. 74 L. 12.02.1979 export exemption' and the customs Movement Reference Number (MRN).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Article 74(1) of the 1979 VAT Law where the SCSp, as exporter of record, dispatches the die-cast scale models to non-EU destinations and proves, by the validated customs export declaration and transport documents, that the goods physically left EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch/procedure acceptance. The exemption also covers supplies placed under export, external transit (T1), customs warehousing and related outward-processing customs regimes. The commercial invoice must cite the statutory exemption, and the goods must be exported directly and without alteration. Luxembourg imposes no separate statutory deadline for repatriation of export proceeds; the 180-day parameter below reflects the standard commercial credit-term benchmark used in transfer-pricing documentation, bank export-financing, and credit insurance facilities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/DAU) validated by the Administration des douanes et accises, bearing the MRN and naming the SCSp as exporter of record.
Transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU within 90 days: negotiable Bill of Lading (sea), CMR consignment note (road), or Air Waybill (air).
Inward Remittance Certificate - bank SWIFT MT103 or credit advice - evidencing receipt of foreign-currency proceeds from the overseas buyer.
Commercial invoice stating the Article 74(1) export exemption, INCOTERMS, quantity, unit price and zero VAT rate for the die-cast collectibles.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT and customs auditors jointly verify MRNs, transport documentation, exit timing and the 90-day exit window. Missing, incomplete or contradictory substantiation triggers retroactive reassessment at the 16% VAT rate with default interest, a surcharge of up to 10% under § 168 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), increasing to 20% for intentional or fraudulent omissions, plus additional fines for failure to produce the SAF-T LS audit file. Forgery of export documents or systematic export-fraud schemes are prosecuted as VAT fraud under the Criminal Code, with substantial fines and imprisonment (up to 5 years); the clawback covers the full VAT amount plus interest rather than only the differential, and input VAT on raw materials may be denied. The general partner (gérant) acting for the fiscally transparent SCSp may be held jointly and severally liable for the VAT debt, and all export records must be retained for at least 10 years under the Commercial Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and AML/CFT controls. Luxembourg applies the EU free movement of capital regime; the BCL administers balance-of-payments statistics, and there is no separate foreign exchange control administration, exchange licensing, or central bank approval requirement for cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Both current-account and capital-account transactions between Luxembourg and non-EU states are unrestricted under Articles 63-65 TFEU, subject only to EU sanctions, standard KYC/AML duties, and CSSF/BCL statistical reporting. Profit remittance from an SCSp to non-resident partners faces no exchange-control hurdle; banks may request underlying documentation and a tax solvency/beneficial-ownership review, but the remittance itself is lawful and can be executed in EUR or foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg does not impose any export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline. Export receipts in USD, CNY, EUR or other currencies may be credited to domestic or foreign accounts freely. The only incidental obligation is the resident bank's reporting of material inward payments to the BCL for monetary and balance-of-payments statistics; no conversion ratio applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as an ancillary payment rail, Medium as the primary treasury vehicle. EEA-licensed E-money Institutions (EMIs) holding a CSSF licence or an MFID/AMLD5 passport may lawfully issue multi-currency IBANs and process SWIFT/PayPal-style settlements, but they do not provide regulated credit, documentary LC, escrow segregation, or FX hedging in the manner of a regulated credit institution. PayPal may be used for collector sales, but it cannot replace banking-grade liquidity management and must itself satisfy EU AML/CFT obligations. All EMIs must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts and are subject to CSSF conduct supervision.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not absolutely require an in-person opening, but in practice, most Tier-1 banks demand a physical meeting with the general partner's authorised manager and, where possible, at least one limited-partner representative. Remote video identification is permitted for natural persons under CSSF AML circulars and the revised Law of 12 November 2004, yet for an SCSp with non-resident limited partners, banks commonly require a signed-notarial qualification or an interview at a Luxembourg branch. The SCSp lacks separate legal personality, so all signatories act via the general partner; the bank may require both the GP and each 25%-plus UBO to produce original passports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp beneficial-ownership opacity: the bank is unable to map the chain of the limited partners and the general partner because the partnership is not a separate legal entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarised or legalised partnership agreement; a certified excerpt of the register of limited partners, prepared by the general partner; the internal UBO register for the SCSp; identification documents (passport) and residence/tax certificates for every natural person owning more than 25% of capital or control; and a CSSF-registered beneficial-owner declaration if one is held.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a non-resident limited partner, especially from outside the EU, raises source-of-funds and sanctions-scope doubts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit bank reference letters from the LP's home bank for the preceding 12 months; three months of source-of-funds bank statements; the capital-call notice and the signed subscription agreement confirming the SCSp stake; tax residence certificates; the LP's commercial registration extract; and a written declaration that the funds do not originate from a listed sanctions-affected jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch: the SCSp is principally a holding/fund vehicle, while the declared business is zinc alloy die-casting and tampo printing of collectible models, creating suspicion of shell activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the Luxembourg registered-office lease or sublease; evidence of physical operations (factory lease, utility bills, machinery invoices, photographs); payroll records for any local employees; signed supplier contracts for zinc ingot, steel/tooling, paints, and packaging; signed customer purchase orders and logotype licences; and customs/export documentation for completed 1:18 scale replicas.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment rails flagged by transaction monitoring: expected PayPal retail inflows and outbound trade wires to Chinese die-casting and tooling suppliers are inconsistent with the SCSp legal form.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a narrative business plan and treasury-flow memorandum: explain that PayPal is used for small-batch collector sales, while B2B raw-material payments move by SWIFT MT103 or irrevocable commercial LC; attach pro-forma invoices from the Chinese suppliers, sea-freight transport documents, the bank's record of supplier due diligence, and copies of the underlying commercial contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must arrive by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT for EUR) to the SCSp's dedicated Luxembourg EUR IBAN held at a CSSF-supervised bank. Field 70 (Remittance Information) should clearly state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO LU_SCSP — PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT [reference]' and use an ISO 20022 payment-purpose code such as 'CAPD' (Capital Payment) or 'INTC' (Intra-company Payment), unless the bank's conventions require 'CUSH' or 'CUST'. The subscribing limited partner must provide proof of identity and source of funds; the general partner must issue a capital-call receipt and update the SCSp's partner register on the same business day. For capital in non-EUR currencies, use a conversion rate confirmed with the receiving bank to avoid wire rejections.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlement, use SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments to zinc alloy ingot, tooling, paint and packaging vendors, particularly in China; use an irrevocable documentary Credit (MT700/MT710, commercial LC at sight) for bulk tooling purchases and ongoing production batches. For LC instructions, the applicant bank in Luxembourg issues the LC in favour of the supplier, with shipping and quality documents requiring inspection at the die-casting facility. PayPal proceeds from collector/customer sales are settled to a dedicated PayPal Business account linked to the SCSp and periodically swept to the Luxembourg operational account by standard withdrawal rail; all PayPal flows are reflected in the same treasury ledger to avoid fragmented audit trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/CNH non-deliverable forwards with maturity matched to trade receivables/payables, executed under an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement or a European Master Agreement with a licensed EU bank
Vanilla FX options (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) for downside protection on export receipts; all options must be plain-vanilla and purchased from a CSSF-licensed investment firm
Cross-currency swaps for term financing, limited to swaps converting USD/CNH-denominated invoices into EUR cash flows
FX spot trading via the commercial bank's e-banking platform with pre-cleared counterparty limits and settlement-date confirmation
Regulated exchange-traded FX futures on Eurex or an EU-regulated venue for micro-hedging of short-term receivables positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (comptes annuels) together with the statutory auditor's report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end and no later than one month after partner approval; for a 31 December year-end, the statutory deadline is 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SCSp and its gérant to administrative and criminal fines up to EUR 25,000; persistent default triggers a formal RCS notice, judicial enforcement, and ultimately administrative strike-off (radiation) with loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership in the RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once each calendar year; where annual accounts are filed, within 30 days after the statutory filing deadline, otherwise no later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or confirm accurate beneficial-ownership data exposes the SCSp to coercive daily fines up to EUR 2,500 per day and fines up to EUR 25,000; deliberate omission may attract criminal liability for the general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, or average workforce exceeding 50 full-time equivalent employees; audit is also required if the partnership agreement mandates it or if an in-kind contribution is certified by a réviseur d'entreprises.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP derived from the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, and the accounting guidance of the Institut des Réviseurs d'Entreprises; IFRS is permissible for non-listed SCSp and mandatory only for listed public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp issues no listed shares; every transfer, subscription, or redemption of partnership interests is evidenced by a written transfer deed and recorded in the register of partners. Such ownership changes must be reported to the RBE within one month. The annual confirmation, filed by the general partner through the LBR electronic portal, certifies that the current beneficial-ownership data is complete and accurate after all partnership interest transfers occurring in the preceding year; the general partner remains continuously responsible for late or inaccurate confirmations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (registre des associés) recording every partnership interest transfer and pledge
Register of Managers / General Partners (rôle des commandités and gérants) recording appointments, revocations, and signature mandates
Minute Book (procès-verbaux) of partner meetings, written resolutions, and capital-account decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 4,000 typical annual registered office and corporate agent fee in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 typical annual fee charged by a Luxembourg-approved réviseur d'entreprises for a small or medium commercial SCSp

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% (plus 7% solidarity surcharge, effective 22.47% for companies; SCSp is fiscally transparent, partners taxed at their own progressive rates)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp itself is not subject to CIT; partners may benefit from Luxembourg's participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains), IP tax regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), and notional interest deduction (NID) for equity investments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) – filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu; for SCSp, a partnership declaration is required, but the entity itself is not subject to CIT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end (standard), with possible extension to 31 March upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp (name, RCS number, address, legal form).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg RCS registration and local tax representative details if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income of the partnership (before allocation to partners).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the partnership's worldwide income; non-resident partners must be identified with their tax residence and share of income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income to each partner (name, address, tax ID, share percentage).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, indicate their country of residence and any treaty provisions affecting taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and allowances (e.g., participation exemption, IP regime, NID).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only applicable if the SCSp has elected to be taxed as a company; otherwise, deductions flow through to partners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: €250 per month, up to €2,500; late payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties up to 10% of tax due for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (standard domestic rate on dividends paid by a Luxembourg company; SCSp distributions are not subject to WHT as the partnership is transparent).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced WHT under a DTA, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residence certificate (TRC) from their home jurisdiction and complete a Luxembourg WHT relief form (Form 105) to the paying agent before the distribution date. For SCSp, no WHT applies; partners report income directly.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% domestic WHT (reduced to 0% under most DTAs if beneficial owner is resident); Interest: 0% domestic WHT (no withholding on interest payments).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if the SCSp's annual turnover exceeds €5 million; Master File required if the group's consolidated turnover exceeds €50 million; CbC report required for groups with consolidated revenue ≥ €750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) to entities carrying on relevant activities (e.g., financing, IP holding). SCSp must demonstrate adequate substance (staff, premises, decision-making) if it is not a pure holding vehicle; otherwise, it may be subject to penalties and recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or failure to file tax returns for the SCSp or its partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties up to 200% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp with no economic substance, no real business activity, and used solely to channel profits or avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, and imposition of 15% WHT on deemed distributions; fines up to €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for restitution of taxes avoided and face disqualification from serving as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining adequate records for the die-cast model business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal sanctions for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally fined and imprisoned if they knowingly facilitate money laundering; travel bans and seizure of personal assets may occur.
